entries.title: The race's weather on the 3D track: sun, cloud and rain in the light, a wet track's sheen, the trees in the wind, and the wind's marker in the world

values.label: the arrow (default): a small ink arrow printed on the paper beside the model, pointing the way the air moved, longer in a stronger wind, with the speed printed under it on a wide screen
the windsock: a striped sock on a pole by the start/finish line, standing out downwind (level by about 17 mph) and fluttering
off: no weather on the models, stills or hover cards (the model as it was)

entries.look: Tracks → Indianapolis Road Course, 2026 · Race 1 (rain, a wet track: greyer light, a sheen on the track, rain falling) against 2025 · Race 1 (clear, an evening sun low in the west); Road America 2024 (17 mph, gusts 35: zoom into the woods to watch them sway); Laguna Seca 2025 · Race 1 (overcast). Turn the model: the arrow and the sheen belong to the world. Press 'Replay this race': the replay's track has the same weather. The years row's stills each carry their own race's weather.

entries.title: The same weather on every race page's 3D track and on the hover cards' stills (the race's own: sky, rain, wind arrow)
entries.look: Race pages: Oulton Park 2020 Race 1 (wet, official), Cadwell Park 2020 Race 2 (19 mph, gusts 44), Portimão 2023 Race 1 (overcast), Hungaroring 2023 Race 2 (clear); an INDY NXT race page, /races/session_indy_nxt_2026_6756 (rain). Hover cards: the Races page's spine dots and Career → The explorer's dots; each card's still carries its race's sky, rain and a small wind arrow. The caption names who called the track wet or dry, by the data's precedence: 'wet track (series report)', 'dry track (observed, NOAA)', 'modelled, Open-Meteo' only where nothing better exists. An observed or reported dry race shows no rain falling (WeatherTech Raceway 2026, Mid-Ohio 2026 Race 2), and the INDY race pages' weather tiles read the same race window and source as the 3D caption. Rain falls over the model only; the wind's words sit by the arrow at every width (on a phone, on a small paper plate where no paper is free).
